**Her sentence, which I want recorded properly:** we bought a project and you sold us a subscription, and for about nine months those looked like the same thing, and then they stopped.

**What we could have done, in her words.** Asked her in about month three what else this was for. She says she would have said nothing, then thought about it and remembered that around 60% of their raw material is imported and that two of their importers asked them last year what they were doing about carbon, because those importers are being asked by their other customers. They were in the middle of a chain and thought they were at the end of one. If that had surfaced in month three, the nine blends would have been the first thing rather than the only thing, and there would have been a second reason to stay when the first one disappeared.

**The onboarding call.** I listened to it again last week. In month one she said, the only reason any of this is happening is one buyer and his template. I wrote it in my notes as background. It was the whole account and I did not hear it.

She asked me directly how many customers look like her. I did not give a number and I said it is most of the ones that look like you, and she said then that is not a churn problem, that is how you sold it. I have nothing to say against that.

**Two things to actually do.** The trigger for a return is most likely one of their importers asking them properly, which she thinks is more likely than their customers, because the pressure is further down the chain and moving up. I have asked her to tell me if it happens and I believe she will. And she is open to being a reference despite having churned, which I did not expect, and which marketing will not know what to do with. Diarised for October, she is in autumn range production until then.
